1. Flow Release 
 
Coast Mountain is committed to providi ng a minimum flow release of 5 m
3/sec 
during the low flow winter months, whic h would increase during the spring and fall 
months along with natural river flows as outlined in table 8.2 of  the Application. A 
copy of this table is provided below.    
 
Coast Mountain recognizes the need to  confirm and further verify the  
information it used when developing its proposed 5 m
3/sec flow regime. To do so we 
are committed to conducting the necessary in-field evaluations, once operations 
begin, to confirm the conclusion and that of its consultants that 5 m 3/sec is sufficient 
to ensure that fish and fish habitat are protected. 
 
Coast Mountain is committed to working with  the responsible regulatory authorities, 
to develop an evaluation or adaptive mana gement program that is acceptable by all 
parties. Considering the uniqueness and cons traints of the of the Iskut Canyon, it will 
be paramount that the program sets out cl early defined objectives and outcomes, as 
well as an acceptable and reasonable means of obtaining the necessary data.  The 
exact content of such a program woul d be subject to detailed and on-going 
discussions with the responsible agencies and Coast Mountain Hydro. 
 
Coast Mountain is confident that the conclu sions it has drawn from all the fieldwork 
and available data on the project to date  will be verified through the evaluation 
program. This has already been partially demonstrated by the work of Dr. Richardson 
on benthic production. In the event that the results of the evaluation program show 
that the release of 5 m
3/sec is adversely affecting aqua tic resources in the diversion 
reach, Coast Mountain is committed to appl ying whatever mitigation strategies or 
further compensation measures are necessa ry to reduce and off-set the potential 
adverse effects. One potential mitigation strategy would be to increase the minimum 
flow release to level that does not exceed 10 m
3/sec.   
 
It should be noted, that Coast Mountain has eval uated the impact of suggested         
16.6 m 3/sec release presented by the regulatory agencies on operations and 
determined that a release of that amount would result with the plant not operating for 
approximately 73 days a year or 20 % of the time. At the proposed 5 m 3/sec the plant 
would not operate on average 5% of the time  or approximately 18 days a year. This 
evaluation was based on Coast Mountains fl ow duration curve mo

2. First Nations 
 
Coast Mountain is committed to continuing its on-going discussions and 
consultations with First Nations representa tives to gain their input on the projects 
development and further define specifi c project components and employment 
opportunities that can be built and fulfilled by First Nation peoples. The local First 
Nations have valuable experience, the necessary personnel and business infrastructure 
to play an important role in the development of Forrest Kerr Project and Coast 
Mountain is committed to ensuring this the case.

3. Project Design Construction 
 
Coast Mountain has presented the proj ect and its proposed  construction in 
Application to the level appropriate for an  environmental assessment level review.  If 
over the course of detailed design and construction planni ng the project significantly 
deviates from that which was presente d in the Application, Coast Mountain is 
committed to ensuring any necessary variances receive the appropriate regulatory 
review.

4. Access Management 
 
Coast Mountain recognizes the concerns over the potential for increased public access 
to remote areas as a result of the projects development.  As such, Coast Mountain is 
committed to maintaining the same level of restricted public access as is currently 
being achieved by Barrick Gold, along the Eskay Creek Mine Road to the project site.  
This restricted access will be maintained  after the Eskay Creek Mine ceases 
permanent operations. 
 
This restricted access will include: 
 
• The maintenance and operation of a keyed gate at its current location. 
• The requirement for the signing of a Ro ad Use Agreement by any member of 
the public not affiliated with the Forrest Kerr Project and its operation before 
access to the road is provided. 
 
Coast Mountain recognizes that during construction activities there will be an 
increase in traffic along the Eskay Creek mine road.  Coast Mountain will be working 
with the operators of the Eskay Creek mine to ensure that restri cted access and safe 
operation of the road is maintained during the two year construction window.

5. Public Access to Information 
 
Coast Mountain recognizes that the members of the public are interested in the 
development of such an important proj ect as the Forrest Kerr hydro-electric 
development, and is committed to ensuring that subsequent studies completed to 
fulfill regulatory requirements are available for public review. However, Coast 
Mountain needs assurance from regulators,  that the public dissemination of such 
material will not be unduly onerous on Co ast Mountain and that information of a 
proprietary nature will be exempt from such a review.

6. Environmental Monitor 
 
As outlined in section 15 of the Applica tion, Coast Mountain is committed retaining 
the services of an indepe ndent environmental monitor to oversee environmental 
aspects of the project over the two year construction window. The qualifications of 
the individual hired to be the monitor as well as the terms of reference for such a 
position, would be mutually agreed to by both Coast Mountain and regulatory 
authorities.  An overview of the terms of reference is provided below: 
 
• Be knowledgeable about all regulatory (environmental) requirements and all 
requirements required by the EA certificates and project permits.
• Be knowledgeable about all of the environmental concerns associated with the 
project and the methods proposed and available to minimize adverse effects; 
• Conduct field evaluations of all areas of potential disturbance, in the core project 
area and along the proposed powerline, to ensure any sensitive or important 
habitats not already identified are avoided and/or the proper mitigation strategies 
are implemented to minimize any potential effects.  
• Relate information to work crews that alerts them to the environmental 
sensitivities that need to be considered while conducting their work; 
• Monitor construction activities along the access road, in the core project area, and 
along the buried and above-ground transmission line.  Provide direction to crews 
on site-specific impact avoidance and mitigation measures.  Ensure 
implementation of mitigation measures;  
• Record and report on environmental matters during project construction to the co.  
Weekly reporting to project managers would be followed, with immediate 
notification of managers and agencies of any significant environmental impacts; 
• Maintain on-site wildlife observation log-books, paying special attention to 
species such as harlequin ducks and furbearers; 
• Provide input to the management of construction activities and work sites to 
minimize unnecessary disturbance to vegetation, streams and other habitat 
features.  Site maintenance would include continuous clean-up and disposal of 
debris, and control of surface runoff to retain sediments and/or hydrocarbon 
products; 
• Have the authority to halt construction activities should he/she determine that 
such activities are significantly impacting the environment; 
• Report any accidents, malfunctions

7. Environmental Management Plan 
 
Coast Mountain recognizes the importance of a solid environmental management plan 
(EMP) and the role it plays in enabling a smooth transition from the projects approval 
through detailed design and into the construc tion and operation of the project.  Coast 
Mountain is committed to developing an EM P in consultation with regulators, that 
sets out the necessary preventative engi neering, mitigation, and monitoring activities 
that will be undertaken during construc tion, operation and decommissioning to 
eliminate adverse effects, offset them or  reduce them to acceptable levels.    An 
outline of Coast Mountain’s proposed EMP was provided in section 15 of the 
Application. It is recognized that the outline presented will require revision and that
several sub-management plans will be re quired to ensure specific concerns are 
adequately addressed, as suggested by the province in their September 25 th 
submission.

8. Rock Chemistry 
 
Although, all studies to date indicate that th ere is very little potential for acid rock 
drainage with the excavated tunnel spoil,  Coast Mountain recognizes the concern and 
need for an appropriate mitigation plan s hould potential acid generating material be 
exposed.  In addition, to conducting further testing and evaluations on any new drilled 
or exposed rock material, Coast M ountain is committed to developing a 
comprehensive, monitoring, materials handl ing and  mitigation plan for excavated 
materials that is acceptable to all parties, prior to construction.

9. Local Hiring 
 
Coast Mountain is committed to maximizing the use of local people when developing 
the Forrest Kerr Project.  To achieve this Coast Mountain Hydro would: 
 
• Include clauses in Construction contracts requiring local advertising for positions. 
• Include clauses in construction contract s requiring training activities for longer-
term projects, such as the two year tunneling program. 
• Include clauses in constr uction contracts ensuring th at local suppliers and 
subcontractors are considered. All supply requirements would be locally obtained 
to the extent possible. 
• Advertise locally for Coast Mountain Hydro’s requirements for caretaker operators 
as required after the plant is operational. 
• Continuing our local public information programs. 
 
The local communities, contractors and individuals in the vicinity of the project, have 
the necessary experience and understanding of the area to be a very valuable resource 
in the successful develo pment of the Forrest Kerr Project. Coast Mountain is 
committed to utilizing this local resource to the maximum extent possible.

1. CMHC must cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed, and 
operated in accordance with the Conditions of this Certificate and the 
documents and correspondence listed in Schedule A, and must comply 
with all of the Conditions of this Certificate to the reasonable satisfaction of 
the Minister.

2. Where, in the reasona ble opinion of the Minister, there is a conflict or 
inconsistency between any of the documents listed in Schedule A and this 
Certificate, Condition 1 must be interpreted so that the contents of the later 
dated document will vary, repeal, rescind or supersede, as the case may 
be, the contents of earlier dated documents listed in Schedule A.

3. Where, in the reasona ble opinion of the Minister, there is a conflict or 
inconsistency between any of the documents listed in Schedule A and the 
Conditions which follow, these Conditions must take precedence over and 
supersede the contents of the documents listed in Schedule A. 
 

4(1). Despite Condition 1 abov e, if prior to the start of operation of the Project, 
CMHC proposes a change to the design, location, construction, operation, 
of the Project as described in the documents listed in Schedule A, and the 
change may in the opinion of the Executive Director, have the potential for 
significant adverse effects, CMHC must then provide the Executive Director 
with: 
a) an application in writin g to amend the Certificate pursuant to section 19 
(1) of the Act.; and 
b) plans, analysis, records and other in formation necessary for an effective 
assessment by the Executive Director of the proposed change. 
 
4(2). Where the Executive Director, or the Minister, following receipt of and 
evaluation of information with respect to an item under Condition 4(1), and 
in consultation with the appropriate authorities, considers that the proposed 
change does not have the potential to cause significant adverse effects, the 
Executive Director, or the Minister, may approve the change to the Project 
and amend this Certificate. 
 
4(3). Where the Executive Director, or the Minister, following receipt of and 
evaluation of information with respect to an item under Condition 4(1), and 
in consultation with the appropriate authorities, considers that the proposed 
change could cause significant adverse effects, the Executive Director, or 
the Minister, may: 
a) establish a review process for an effective assessment of the potential 
effects of the change and cause it to be conducted; 
b) on conclusion of the review proc ess, make a decision regarding the 
proposed change to the Project and add, vary or delete conditions to the 
Certificate considered necessary; and 
 
4(4). The Executive Director must deliv er the decision with respect to an 
amendment under this Condition to CMHC.

5. CMHC to maintain at all times a minimum flow of 16.6 cms (6% Mean 
Annual Discharge) in the Iskut River, measured immediately downstream of 
the power tunnel intake located near the confluence of the Iskut River and 
Forrest Kerr Creek, unless CMHC can demonstrate, to the reasonable 
satisfaction of the Comptroller of Water Rights in consultation with fisheries 
agencies, that another minimum flow can adequately protect fisheries 
values on the following basis: 
a) through new information provided by CMHC prior to Project 
construction, or 
 

b) following Project constructi on, through an adaptive management 
program carried out by CMHC in the manner described in section 
5.1.1.1 of the Forrest Kerr Hydroelectric Project Assessment Report; or 
c) because of natural flows.

6. CMHC should make bona fide effort s to attempt to reach an agreement 
with the Iskut and Tahltan First Nations to address their outstanding 
concerns, and make quarterly reports to the EAO describing those attempts 
until such time as an agreement is reached, or until relieved of the 
obligation by the Executive Director.

7. CMHC must cause the Project to be constructed and operated in 
accordance with the documents and correspondence listed in Schedule A.  
Where there is a conflict or inconsistency between commitments made in 
the documents or correspondence listed in Schedule A, the commitments 
of the later dated document will supersede the commitments of the earlier 
dated document.

8. CMHC must develop, prior to the st art of construction and in consultation 
with the Department of Fisheries and Oceans, the Canadian Wildlife 
Service, Land and Water BC Inc. (LWBC), and the Iskut and Tahltan First 
Nations, the environmental management commitments described in the 
documents listed in Schedule A, as well as the Component Plans identified 
in s. 5.1.6 of the Assessment Report, to the reasonable satisfaction of the 
Comptroller of Water Rights (LWBC Inc.), the Director of Regional 
Operations, Environmental Protection Division and the Director of Regional 
Operations, Environmental Stewardship Division of the Ministry of Water, 
Land and Air Protection (WLAP), and implement them.

9. CMHC must develop, in consultation with the Director of Regional 
Operations, Environmental Protection Division and the Director of Regional 
Operations, Environmental Stewardship Division (WLAP), Comptroller of 
Water Rights (LWBC Inc.), and the Iskut and Tahltan First Nations, a Fish 
Habitat Compensation Plan consistent with commitments made in the 
Application and documents listed in Schedule A, to the reasonable 
satisfaction of the Chief, Major Projects Review Unit, Habitat and 
Enforcement Branch, Department of Fisheries and Oceans, Pacific Region, 
and implement them.

12. CMHC must, except in connection with granting security to Project lenders 
or other financing entities or financing facilities, obtain the written consent 
of the Minister, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, prior to 
disposing, whether legally, beneficially or otherwise, of: 
 
a) this Certificate, or any right, title or  interest conferred by this Certificate, 
or  
b) the Project.

13. CMHC must have, in the reasonable opinion of the Minister, substantially 
started the Project within five years of the date of issue of this Certificate.

14. CMHC, in addition to the Condition # 6, must submit written reports on the 
status of compliance with the Conditions of this Certificate to the EAO: 
 
a) three months prior to the start of construction; 
b) every six months after the beginning of construction until the start of 
Project operation; and 
c) annually for five years after the start of operations or until relieved of the 
obligation by the Executive Director.

3.   Terrestrial Resources
3.1  Terrestrial  Clearing and construction within the Ningunsaw and 
Estshi floodplains will occur between June 15 
th  and 
November 15 th  to avoid critical periods for moose 
(November 15 th -May 15 th ) and grizzly bear (April 15 th  – 
June 15 th ).  
EA Amendment 5  MoE EA Commitment

3.2  Terrestrial  Project related low level aerial flights, in the Ni ngunsaw 
and Estshi flood plains during the critical periods  for 
moose and grizzly bear (dates above) will be limite d to 
flights specifically required for the installation and 
maintenance of the Transmission Line  
EA Amendment 5  MoE EA Commitment

3.3  Terrestrial  CMHC will conduct a winter goat observation program in 
winter 2010 to better understand their use of the h abitat 
within 500m of Estshi Creek.  
EA Amendment 5  MoE EA Commitment

3.4  Terrestrial  CMHC will conduct additional call/playback surveys for 
Northern Goshawk, prior to clearing of the transmis sion 
line right of way (ROW). If an active nest is found , 
CMHC will implement clearing restrictions, to be 
developed in consultation with a qualified professi onal, 
on a site specific basis depending on the location within 
the project and clearing needs at the site. 
 
EA Amendment 5  MoE Wildlife Act Permit

3.5  Terrestrial  Clearing that is required in deciduous stands will be 
scheduled to avoid the May 15 th  to July 30 th  breeding 
and fledging period for migratory birds. If clearin g is 
required between May 15 th  to July 30 th    a qualified 
professional will assess the area for nests and mitigation 
strategies prior to clearing.  
EA Amendment 5  MoE Wildlife Act Permit

3.6  Terrestrial  Coarse woody debris piles will be installed in the 
Transmission line ROW as habitat features for Marten. 
 
EA Amendment 5  MoE EA Commitment

CMHC recognizes that Tahltan have various land use interests in the vicinity of the Project, and will continue to engage and discuss with the Tahltan, through THREAT, to discuss their interests, issues and identify mitigation measures required to ensure that where practicable, all land and resource uses remain available in the future.

If archaeological sites are identified within defined work areas, CMHC will work with Tahltan (through the Forrest Kerr Environmental Performance Committee) and the Archaeology Branch to best determine mitigation.

CMHC will finalize revisions to the Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) in consultation with Agencies and the THREAT, prior to construction. The Engineering Procurement and Construction Management (EPCM) firm, (maintains overall site responsibility during construction) and subcontractors on site during construction will be required to comply with the CEMP and all the associated plans. As follows:
• Access Management Plan
• Fuelling, Fuel Storage and Equipment Maintenance
• Material and Waste Management
• Invasive Plant Control Management Plan
• Waste Rock Management Plan
• Wildlife Management Plan
• Spill Contingency and Emergency Response Plan
• Sediment and Erosion Control Management Plan
• Cultural and Heritage Site Protection
• Reclamation Management Plan
CMHC will develop and implement an Operational Environmental Management Plan by Commercial Operation Date (COD).

CMHC commits to undertake an Effects Assessment of Ramping Associated with a Major Unscheduled Outage, as described in the Work Plan submitted to Agencies on February 17th, 2010. The information from this study will be combined with the information in the report “Potential effects of ramping on overwintering bull trout in the diversion reach” January 25, 2010, to create an overall Management Plan for flow ramping during an emergency shutdown.
